objective: Provide source-aligned PowerShell, JavaScript, Node.js, C#, .NET, Python, and Azure service guidance for the Launch Pad and stack-aware generated/adopted projects without new runtime dependencies.

context.versionPolicy: Preserve each project's supported versions, module format, SDK/TFM policy, formatter, and CI matrix. Reverify official lifecycle and API guidance before upgrades; no runtime or SDK versions were changed.
context.productionNodeRecommendation: Prefer Active or Maintenance LTS; framework compatibility and production LTS recommendations are distinct.
context.cloudPolicy: Reuse the saved project cloud and verify service-specific endpoint, API, model, quota, and feature availability. Documentation is not subscription or deployment evidence.

coverage.conclusion: Language-level module compatibility, explicit absence/coercion, promise/error handling, resource cleanup, boundary validation, and TypeScript narrowing without forcing JavaScript projects to adopt TypeScript.

Strict checking strengthens static checks; TypeScript upgrades may introduce additional diagnostics and do not replace runtime validation.

coverage.conclusion: Dedicated runtime guidance separates production LTS selection from compatibility, protects the event loop, bounds resources/processes, handles shutdown, and preserves reproducible dependency installation.

references.supports: Production applications should use Active or Maintenance LTS. Do not copy a temporary latest-version label into permanent policy.
Application-level limits, dependency trust, lockfiles, CI installs, unsafe object merges, and debug-interface exposure.
Nonblocking request work, bounded input/CPU complexity, and the distinction between server hot paths and bounded CLI/startup work.

coverage.conclusion: Language/API conventions respect the existing style and compiler support, preserve nullable analysis, propagate async cancellation, and dispose only owned resources.

references.supports: Microsoft explicitly describes its documentation/sample conventions as adaptable examples, not a universal authoritative style mandate.
Readable, isolated, repeatable behavior tests; coverage alone does not demonstrate test or code quality.

provisioning.compatibilityNote: Reuse the existing csharp stack tag for .NET project files, including F#/VB project files; do not impose C# language rules on other .NET languages.

coverage.conclusion: Separate SDK/TFM, dependency, analyzer, DI/hosting, cancellation, and HTTP-lifetime guidance corrects the former factory-only HttpClient rule.

references.supports: SDK and runtime versioning are distinct; runtime upgrades still require compatibility assessment and retesting.
Both factory-created short-lived clients and appropriately pooled long-lived clients are documented strategies; evaluate DNS and cookie-container ownership.
Keep infrastructure-dependent integration checks separate from deterministic unit tests.

coverage.conclusion: Add first-class Python conventions, environment isolation, supported-interpreter compatibility, verified typing, structured exceptions, context-managed resources, and project-selected testing/linting.

references.supports: Readable conventions, explicit absence, specific exceptions, resource management, and preserving local style and backward compatibility rather than applying style mechanically.
Project-isolated environments and explicit package/dependency management; examples do not authorize installations or a particular supported-version floor.

provisioning.applicationSdkRouting: The shared best-practices router explicitly applies service guidance to SDK work outside infra/.

coverage.conclusion: Cover five-pillar tradeoffs, identity and least privilege, bounded transport behavior, redacted observability, data/network controls, discovery evidence, and cloud-specific availability without enabling Azure MCP or performing remote operations.

references.supports: Reliability, Security, Cost Optimization, Operational Excellence, and Performance Efficiency require workload-specific design tradeoffs and review.
Use documented SDK pipelines, redacted diagnostics, correlation, and mockable/offline tests. SDK-author parameter-validation guidance does not remove application-boundary validation requirements.
Endpoints, feature configuration, and availability can differ between Azure Government and global Azure; confirm the selected service and cloud instead of copying public-cloud assumptions.
